notes: Diagnosis and fix of the qa023_brute_2x2 node-budget alarm (T360's still-open diagnosis). ROOT CAUSE: the original brute_value rejected only repeats along the current DFS path, so it enumerated simple paths, not states. On 2x2 the basic-ko shape never fires (the goban is too small), so capture-recapture cycles are unbounded by the rule and only the path history stops them; simple paths in the 2430-state 2x2 graph run to depth ~40-50 before a state repeats (measured: depth_limit_hits==0, so the depth bound never even fired) and there are exponentially many of them. The search spun at 100% CPU for up to 171 min; T360 turned the spin into a @panic on a 20M-node budget, which was the signal not the cure. SECONDARY DEFECT FOUND: the path-history DFS is also UNSOUND, not merely slow — its value is path-dependent (a state reached with different ancestors can yield a different value, because a cycle back to an ancestor is TIE on one path and not on another). A memoised on-stack DFS was tried first: it collapsed the count and reproduced five anchors but returned the WRONG value on the ko-shape smoke test, because the memo freezes a value from one stack context and reuses it in another. FIX: replaced the DFS with the L/H median fixpoint (the same sound algorithm exp6_solve.zig's run_fixpoint_2x2 uses) — seed terminals (passes==2) with area score, give every other state widest bounds L=-4/H=+4, sweep (Black: L=max child L, H=max child H; White: min/min) until stable, resolve v=max(L,min(TIE,H)). Monotone over the finite [-4,4] lattice => converges in a handful of passes over 2430 states, microseconds, no budget, no path dependence. NODE_BUDGET/nodes_visited removed (search finite by construction => T360 alarm obsolete). Fingerprint/fp_eq retained as named records. RESULT: zig test -O ReleaseSafe src/qa023_brute_2x2.zig -> 84 passed; 0 skipped; 1 failed; ZERO crashes (all four qa023 panics gone). 3 of the 4 previously-crashing smoke tests now pass with correct values (empty B=0, empty W=0, passes=1=0); full B=4, full W=-4, passes=2=0 also pass. The 4th crashing test ('1-ko shape') no longer crashes but FAILS on a pre-existing WRONG ASSERTION: it asserts value 0 but the true value is -4 (White to move at [-1,1,0,0] captures the lone Black stone by playing cell 3; basic ko never fires on 2x2 so Black has no recapture ban and is reduced to passing; terminal area score = -4). This was never observed before because the test always panicked before reaching the assertion. Verified against the AUTHORITATIVE exp6_solve.zig run_fixpoint_2x2 (also L=-4 H=-4 v=-4, converged in 4 sweeps) and by hand analysis. PER THE BRIEF ('If the only way to make the red go away is to change what the test measures, stop and report that instead — the row is then a design question for the Orchestrator'), the assertion was NOT changed. DESIGN QUESTION FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: correct the ko-shape smoke test's expected value from 0 to -4 (or reframe the test); it is the true draw-on-repetition value, confirmed by the authoritative solver. CONSUMERS UNCHANGED: exp6_solve/exp4_solve/exp5_solve/exp6_hchain_audit/audit_2x2_mismatch/differential/qa023_probe/ko_probe all compile unchanged against the modified file (they use State/apply_place/apply_pass/global_index/state_from_index/board_index/mark_reachable/TOTAL_STATES, none of which changed; the removed symbols brute_value/nodes_visited/NODE_BUDGET/UNCOMPUTED/FP_STACK_SIZE had no external references). keybyte_differential has a pre-existing build-wiring error (missing 'engine' module via build.zig import_table) identical with and without this change — not caused by this task. Acceptance gate is RED only on the ko-shape wrong-assertion, which is a design question and was left per the brief. Matched-test count asserted: 85 tests in the file (7 smoke + 78 inherited from rules/state/terminal via the import), 84 pass, 1 fail, 0 crash. No managent directives were pending for T452 (inbox empty at every checkpoint).
